auto_false_positive.reason: STUN binding request/response - normal NAT traversal traffic, used by Tailscale, WebRTC, VoIP, gaming.

Legacy ET MALWARE Conficker/KEYPLUG P2P UDP signatures (2009-era) match modern STUN traffic to Microsoft Azure STUN servers (20.202.0.0/16:3478) used by Teams, Xbox Live, Skype, and other Microsoft services for NAT traversal. Confirmed false positive: same UDP packet shape, different intent. The LLM consistently misclassifies these because the signature description biases toward 'malware' without port-aware context. Manual review confirms benign — port 3478 is IANA-assigned STUN.
STUN binding on non-standard high port - same NAT traversal mechanism, different rule pattern.
DNS NXDOMAIN response - benign DNS lookup failure (typo'd domains, browser prefetch, Pi-hole blocks). DGA-style abuse is caught separately by SID 2008470.
Go HTTP client user agent - normal traffic from Go-based services in the homelab (containers, internal tools, CI/CD agents).
Discord chat service traffic - normal Discord usage from desktop/mobile clients.

Suricata decoder event for unknown EtherType - emitted when Suricata sees layer-2 frames it can't classify (often VLAN tags, MPLS, IPv6 extensions, or vendor-specific protocols). Decoder noise, not a security signal. Confirmed across thousands of samples in homelab traffic — 100% false positive rate via LLM classification.
Spotify P2P client traffic - normal Spotify desktop client peer-to-peer caching behavior.
Linux APT user-agent outbound - normal package update traffic (apt update / apt upgrade) from homelab Linux servers.
Python BaseHTTP server banner - homelab Python services exposing their default banner. Internal traffic, not an exposure risk on a private network.
